issues.legal_issue: A bank may not reverse a credit correctly made to a constituent’s account for money paid on the constituent’s behalf merely because the payer made the payment by mistake, unless the constituent consents.
material_facts: A borrower’s loan was to be repaid through amounts collected by the government and sent to the bank for credit to the borrower’s account.
For several years, both the treasury and the Accountant General mistakenly sent payment instruments for the same amounts, resulting in duplicate credits to the borrower’s account.
The bank had received the money for credit to the borrower’s account and had correctly entered the amounts shown in the payment instruments.
At the Accountant General’s request, and without the borrower’s consent, the bank reversed the credits and then sought to recover the increased balance from the borrower’s successors.
issues.conclusion: The bank was not entitled to reverse the credits without the constituent’s consent. Section 72 did not apply to permit the bank to return the money from the constituent’s account to the payer; the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 72 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 applies where one person pays money to another who receives it on the payer’s behalf. It does not apply where money is paid to a bank with instructions to credit a third-party constituent’s account. Once correctly credited, the money belongs to the constituent, and the bank cannot debit it or reverse the credit without the constituent’s authority. The payer may seek recovery from the constituent. Imperial Bank of Canada v. Bank of Hamilton, L.R. [1903] A.C. 49, was distinguished because it concerned a mistaken payment between banks and did not involve reversal of an entry in a constituent’s account.

rule.if: bank_debt_recovery_case and payment_for_constituent and credit_matches_payment_instructions and payer_made_duplicate_payment and bank_reversed_credit_without_constituent_consent

predicates.bank_debt_recovery_case: The proceeding concerns a bank’s claim to recover a debt from a borrower or the borrower’s successors.
predicates.payment_for_constituent: A payer sent money to the bank with instructions that it be credited to a constituent’s account.
predicates.credit_matches_payment_instructions: The bank credited the constituent’s account with the amount it received in accordance with the payment instructions.
predicates.payer_made_duplicate_payment: The payer mistakenly sent payment more than once for the same obligation.
predicates.bank_reversed_credit_without_constituent: The bank reversed the credit at the payer’s request without obtaining the constituent’s consent.

issues.definition: When a bank seeks to recover a debt after reversing a correctly instructed credit made for a constituent because of the payer’s duplicate payment, and the constituent did not consent, the bank cannot reverse that credit without the constituent’s consent.
